Poisson algebras via model theory and differential-algebraic geometry — Jason Bell, Stéphane Launois, Omar León Sánchez and Rahim Moosa; Journal of the European Mathematical Society 19(7) (2017),2019–2049. Prior negative answers in every Krull dimension d≥4: Theorem 4.1, Proposition 5.2 and Corollary 5.3 yield a complex affine integral Poisson algebra with 0 rational but not locally closed; Theorem 3.2 makes 0 primitive. Localization proves its maximal-spectrum core is dense; the Jacobson/Poisson-prime intersection criterion shows that core cannot be locally closed. This is an explicit checked deduction to Brown’s original MaxA question, not a literal claim that Corollary 5.3 names symplectic cores. No all-prime-core assertion or classification of positive subclasses. Published JEMS PDF inspected; separate LWW arXiv v2 all-prime wording is not used. row: 3100034 / AMR-030-0034 — Cooper's perfectly k-symmetric permutations: exact equal counts of all subsequence patterns; https://people.math.sc.edu/cooper/combprob.html

Gal Beniamini, Nir Lavee and Nati Linial, How Balanced Can Permutations Be?, Combinatorica 45, article 9 (2025), published online 2 January 2025. Full finite classification for integers n>=k>=1: k=1 all n; k=2 iff n mod4 is0 or1; k=3 iff n mod36 is0,1,9,20,28,29; k>=4 none. Thus infinitely many lengths for each k<=3 and none for k>=4. Patterns use arbitrary increasing index sets, not consecutive substrings. Theorems1–2 and Theorem5; exceptional19 witnesses in AppendixA Table1. Existing published resolution, not a new project theorem or upload. Audited in PR1194: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1194 .
